title: Swage Press
pages: Craft the controller with plain pistons, gold ingots and a Forming Die: hand-finish Quench Vat tempered steel with flint and a grindstone. It is a 3x3x3 rotary swager (22 blocks plus the controller); build it from the bottom up. Layer 1, the cast bed, is a gold block directly beneath the controller (the fixed die block) ringed by eight smooth stone. Layer 2 holds the controller with a plain piston on its north and south sides facing inward toward it (the hammer dies) and a polished andesite post in each corner; the east and west sides stay open for feeding. Layer 3, the head, is a grindstone flywheel directly above the controller, smooth stone crossbeams over each hammer piston and polished andesite caps on the four corner posts. A Structure Projector bound to the controller shows each layer in turn. The crafted Forming Die occupies the centre of the controller recipe; it is a consumable construction part, not a replacement for the gold die block in the formed structure. Material update: crafting slot 2 (row-major 3x3) now requires a vanadium ingot via forge:ingots/vanadium; all existing progression gates remain required.

Right-click the controller with feedstock from a loaded swaging recipe. The press loads one recipe batch into its stock buffer, processes it over 40 ticks, and holds the output for empty-hand collection or bottom-face extraction. A missing gold die, bed or crossbeam block, corner post, grindstone flywheel, or an outward/missing hammer piston stops operation without consuming items. Plain stone does not replace smooth stone and raw andesite does not replace polished andesite. Two presses may share a bed or post block; the lower-position controller owns it and the other press stays unformed until that controller is removed.

The formed press runs 21 exclusive datapack swaging batches in 40 ticks each. Four iron ingots, or advanced stock such as annealed copper, tempered steel and sealed steel plate, still form the Swaged Fitting needed for the Press; one Bearing Steel Stock forms two Bearing Race Blanks for the Magnetizer bearing route. The rotary dies also draw four gold ingots into golden horse armor, which no crafting table can make, and three copper ingots into a lightning rod. Nine iron or gold nuggets compact into one ingot, while nine raw iron, raw gold, raw copper, or coal compact into their matching storage block. Ore-line metals (matched by forge:ingots tags) swage into hardware: two thallium make a chain, two bismuth make shears, two palladium make a heavy weighted pressure plate, six rhodium make sixteen rails, and iridium (3), ruthenium (3), niobium (2) and vanadium (1) forge an iron-grade pickaxe, axe, sword and shovel. These batches cost at least the material of the equivalent vanilla crafts and make hopper-fed stock handling useful. Right-click a formed controller with the input to load one batch; empty-hand right-click collects output. The press uses no FE.

Two swaged fittings fill opposite corners of the Press craft. The Press craft is now a swaged fitting, tempered steel and a Temper Glyph on top, tempered steel either side of a piston, then a riveted brace, tempered steel and a second swaged fitting along the bottom. The Swage Press is a required pressing-tier apparatus; a bare iron ingot does not substitute for either fitting.

Automation: place a hopper or item pipe against any input face (all faces except the bottom by default) and feed a loaded recipe input. A formed controller processes one batch every 40 ticks without FE; its bottom face outputs to a hopper or pipe. Empty-hand right-click collects buffered products. Sneak-right-click a face with an empty hand cycles it through input, output and off. Full output pauses processing; broken or unloaded structures do not process. Buffered items and side settings survive saving; breaking the controller drops its buffers.
